title: Honor unattended mode in orphan package review
head: 34686e75ba35
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: The new interactive assertion inherits an ambient unattended flag and can report a false regression
leads.consequence: When this test is launched with OMARCHY_UPDATE_UNATTENDED=1 already exported, the second script invocation inherits that value, correctly skips gum, and fails the assertion that interactive review still prompts. Set OMARCHY_UPDATE_UNATTENDED=0 (or remove it with env -u) explicitly for the interactive invocation. This is an environmental test-isolation issue, not a failure of the new orphan command under -y; another pre-existing update-sequence test also assumes the flag is absent.
leads.triage: already_in_opus_final; Opus reproduced (exit 1 with =1); published as Optional test improvement; fix verified by Opus run d6aa4702

leads.summary: Two open PRs already edit the identical orphan guard
leads.consequence: Both open PRs replace the same baseline guard with an unattended check. #8824 and #9511 spell the default differently from this head (:- versus :-0), so merging either independently against the other needs a choice at this hunk, and their PTY coverage duplicates the new test. The intended runtime result is equivalent for absent and 1 values; this is integration conflict/redundant coverage, not proof of a newly broken update.
leads.triage: already_in_opus_final; coordinator verified via read-only gh: #8824 open/clean, #9511 open/dirty, #8894 closed unmerged, #8780 open; #9511 patch touches migration; published

leads.summary: A failed orphan query is indistinguishable from no orphans (pre-existing)
leads.consequence: If pacman -Qtdq is unavailable or errors without producing stdout, its diagnostics and nonzero status are swallowed; the script exits successfully and prints nothing, concealing that orphan review did not occur. The baseline has exactly the same lines, so this is a pre-existing input-error boundary and not caused by this PR. Distinguishing pacman's normal no-match status from genuine query failures would require pacman-specific status handling.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** under `omarchy update -y`, the orphan step now reports the orphans and continues instead of stopping at `gum confirm`. Runs without `-y` still reach the confirmation prompt, and the new test fails on the base and passes on this head. No defect was found in the diff. The same one-line fix is also open in #8824 and in #9511 (details below).

**Verified:** On entry, `omarchy-update` re-runs itself under `script -qefc` (`bin/omarchy-update:86-89`), and `script` gives the child a PTY on fds 0, 1 and 2 even when the caller's stdin is not a terminal. That is why the old `-t` guard never fired inside an update. `-y` exports `OMARCHY_UPDATE_UNATTENDED=1` at `:103`, after the re-execs and before the orphan step at `:130`. The run below used the real `bin/omarchy-update`, its real `script` re-exec and the real orphan step, with caller stdin `/dev/null` and stub `pacman`/`gum`. Every other update step was replaced by the repository's logging stand-ins (`test/shell.d/fixtures/sudo-boundary-test.sh`), and in the no-`-y` runs the confirmation step was a stand-in that answered yes:

| Run | Base (`c5b4db77`) | This PR (`34686e75`) |
|---|---|---|
| `-y` | `gum confirm --default=false Remove 2 orphaned package(s)?` with tty0/1/2 all true and `OMARCHY_UPDATE_UNATTENDED=1` | no `gum` call, prints `2 orphaned package(s) found. Re-run omarchy-update-orphan-pkgs in a terminal to review/remove them.`, update exits 0 and runs the later steps |
| no `-y` | reaches `gum confirm` | reaches `gum confirm` (unchanged) |

Only the exact value `1` skips the prompt, which matches `omarchy-update-restart:14` and `omarchy-update-system-pkgs-when-conflicted:74`. The result also matches what `docs/update-process.md:161` already documents for `-y`. One visible side effect: `omarchy-channel-set` finishes with `omarchy-update -y` (`:150`), so channel switches now skip the orphan prompt too. That is consistent with the same `-y` contract.

### Same fix already open in #8824 and #9511

#8824 (open since 2026-08-28) changes the same guard on `bin/omarchy-update-orphan-pkgs:15` to `${OMARCHY_UPDATE_UNATTENDED:-} == 1` and extends the existing `test/shell.d/update-orphan-test.sh`. #9511 (open, currently conflicting with `quattro`) contains the same guard change as part of a broader `--yes` rework. #8894 made the same change and was closed without merging. The bug was first reported in #8780. #13356 reports it again.

**Impact:** the PRs conflict textually on that one line. Whichever lands first leaves the others to be rebased or closed. The two guards behaved the same for every variable value tested (unset, empty, `0`, `1`, `true`, `yes` and padded forms). This PR's test adds an interactive-path check that the #8824 test does not have.

**Suggested change:** reference #8824, #9511 and #8780 in the PR description, so maintainers can pick one version and close the related issues together.

### Another `gum confirm` in the `-y` path (outside this diff)

`migrations/1786643346.sh:169-170` loops on `gum confirm "Close the browser windows ..."` while an affected browser profile is open, and it does not check `OMARCHY_UPDATE_UNATTENDED`. `omarchy-migrate` runs at `bin/omarchy-update:129`, one step before the orphan step, under the same PTY. So `omarchy update -y` can still wait at a prompt when that migration is pending and an affected Chromium-family profile is open. The migration's comment expects gum to fail "without a terminal to ask in", but under `script` a terminal is present. In a sandboxed run of the real `omarchy-update -y`, `omarchy-migrate` and this migration, with a synthetic browser profile holding a `SingletonLock` and a stub `gum`, the migration reached `gum confirm Close the browser windows to repair the Copy URL shortcut, then continue` with stdin and stdout on a TTY and `OMARCHY_UPDATE_UNATTENDED=1`. Without the lock, the repair ran and the update finished. The real gum wait itself was not run.

**Impact:** a narrow case of the same hang that #13356 describes. It is not limited to one run: the migration is marked done only on success, so the prompt can return on every `-y` run until the repair completes. The issue asks that "any other step calling gum" get the same treatment.

**Suggested change:** guard that prompt the same way, either here or in a follow-up. #9511 already does this with `[[ ${OMARCHY_UPDATE_UNATTENDED:-} == 1 ]] || ! gum confirm ...`. That takes the existing decline path: the migration exits 1 and stays pending, and `omarchy update -y` stops at the migration step with its error message instead of waiting, so the orphan step and later steps do not run. #9511 intends that outcome ("fail with an actionable message instead of waiting").

**Optional test improvement:** the interactive case in `test/shell.d/update-orphan-pkgs-test.sh` does not clear `OMARCHY_UPDATE_UNATTENDED`. When the test runs with `OMARCHY_UPDATE_UNATTENDED=1` already exported, it fails at `interactive orphan review still prompts`, even though the script behaves correctly. Adding `OMARCHY_UPDATE_UNATTENDED=0` to the second `script` invocation makes the test pass with the variable already exported, and it still fails against the base script.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** source review of the full `omarchy-update` step sequence, the orphan step, the related PRs and issues, and upstream util-linux `script` and gum `confirm` sources. Sandboxed runs used stub `pacman`, `gum` and `sudo` with no real package operations. They covered the new test on head and base, diagnostic mutants of the guard, a value matrix for the variable, the end-to-end `omarchy-update` run shown above, and the migration prompt with a synthetic browser profile. The real gum TUI wait was not run; that conclusion rests on the gum source and the reports in #13356 and #8780. `test/shell.d/update-lock-test.sh` could not run in the sandbox on either base or head, and it does not exercise the changed step.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
